title: PeakData x Redwood - Migration demo (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked PeakData through API parity mapping from their current OpenAI/Anthropic/Together setup to Redwood. Demo covered endpoint parity, streaming, function/tool-calling, embeddings migration, Console rollout and Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization). Customer raised questions on latency differences, VPC and KMS, SOC2 compliance, and data residency. Agreed next steps: share parity mapping doc + migration checklist, schedule performance benchmark (pilot), and provide pricing for Dedicated capacity options.
action_items: Maya Patel — send parity mapping doc + sample request/response mappings by 2026-04-02
Jonas Reed — prepare benchmark plan (latency & cost) and test harness details by 2026-04-07
Sofia Alvarez (PeakData) — share representative prompt set and traffic profile by 2026-04-03
Ben Price (PeakData) — confirm VPC requirements and allowed CIDR ranges by 2026-04-06
next_steps: Redwood to share parity mapping spreadsheet and migration checklist
Schedule 2-hour pilot kickoff next week to run throughput/latency benchmarks
Provide Dedicated pricing options and estimated monthly cost from Optimize suggestions
Share SOC2 + security pack and KMS integration notes
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're excited to walk through how PeakData can migrate from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood with minimal changes. Um, quick intros — Jonas from Solutions/SE, Lina on solutions.
[00:12] Arjun (CTO): Thanks Maya. We're mostly trying to get parity on model behaviour and function calling, and we run a mix of embeddings and chat generation.
[00:23] Jonas (SE): Great, we'll show the API parity patterns first, then Console and Optimize. Quick note — some of the names in the transcript may be off, apologies, and there might be minor transcription errors.
[00:35] Sofia (ML Eng): Sounds good. Our main constraints: latency under 150ms p50 on short prompts, cost targets, and we need VPC/private deployment for PHI pipelines.
[00:48] Maya: Okay got it. So first, API parity — Redwood exposes similar REST endpoints, e.g., /v1/generate (parity to chat completions), /v1/embeddings, and we also support streaming and tool calling. Here's a sample mapping doc — we will send it after the call.
[01:06] Ben (Infra): What about function calling? We rely heavily on structured tool calls from the model and the sequential function signature behaviour from Anthropic and OpenAI.
[01:16] Jonas: We implemented function/tool calling with the same intent/arguments pattern. Implementation detail: Redwood handles tool calls as structured JSON in the stream, and the SDK deserializes into the tool call with name/args. There are small differences in how we annotate provenance, but behavior can be made identical by mapping a small wrapper in your client.
[01:36] Tasha (PM): Are there known divergences with Together models? They do a lot of safety filtering at the model layer.
[01:43] Jonas: Good point — behavior depends on model variant. For parity we recommend selecting Redwood-verified model variants that match the same safety/profile and then applying the same prompt engineering layers. Redwood Optimize can recommend a variant and quantization profile to match cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:00] Arjun: Streaming is big for us — we stream partial results to our UI. Does Redwood support chunked tokens and delta streaming?
[02:08] Maya: Yes, streaming is first-class. We return token deltas, stream events for function calls, and you can subscribe via server-sent events or websockets. The behavior mirrors OpenAI streaming patterns; we will include sample code.
[02:20] Sofia: How about embeddings? We compute 512-d vectors with OpenAI now; can we map to Redwood embeddings without retraining downstream indexes?
[02:30] Jonas: Embedding parity is trickier — you might see distributional shifts. We recommend a validation run: compute embeddings on a representative corpus and run nearest-neighbor recall. Usually Redwood's open-model embeddings are within tolerances, but if you require exact parity we can run the seeded pilot and optionally run an index-rewrite plan.
[02:54] Ben: Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS — for our regulated workflows we need tenant-managed keys.
[03:03] Lina: Redwood Private supports KMS integrations (customer-managed keys), audit logs, RBAC and SAML SSO. For on-prem or VPC we can run the control plane with your network. We'll attach the security pack that lists SOC2/ISO cert status.
[03:20] Arjun: How about KV cache behavior and long-context models — our sessions rely on cached KV to keep context cheap.
[03:29] Jonas: Our runtime exposes KV cache controls; when you pin model versions we maintain the cache and we also support persistent prefix caching for repeated sessions. There are some differences in eviction policies vs your current provider, but they are tunable.
[03:47] Tasha: Cost — do you have guidelines for quantization vs accuracy?
[03:51] Jonas: Yes — Redwood Optimize will run your workload stats and recommend quantization (8-bit, 4-bit) and batching levels. For many production workloads, 4-bit quant with per-layer calibration preserves quality while reducing GPU memory by ~40-60% — but we always recommend running your prompt set against candidate models before rollout.
[04:16] Sofia: Any gotchas on SDK changes? We use a thin wrapper today that does retries, rate limiting, and backoff.
[04:22] Maya: SDKs are similar; you can keep your wrapper. Auth is done with bearer tokens and we support short-lived tokens via your platform. For VPC/private deployments you can also authenticate via mutual TLS.
[04:34] [05:00] Demo: Jonas screenshares the Console. Jonas: Here is the per-model latency/cost dashboard, token breakdown, and the rollout controls. You can create a canary and route 10% of traffic to a new variant.
[05:20] Sofia: Nice — can we create route-based policies (by endpoint or path)?
[05:24] Jonas: Yep, route-based routing and policy rules; you can route by model, latency SLO, or region.
[05:32] Maya: For migration we usually recommend: 1) parity mapping, 2) small pilot (1-2 endpoints), 3) run Optimize — collect perf & cost stats, 4) canary rollout, 5) full cutover.
[05:48] Arjun: For the pilot, what's a typical timeline?
[05:51] Maya: Two weeks for a basic bench and integration, 4-6 weeks if you want full-scale rewrites and index migration. We'll scope in the benchmark plan.
[06:04] Ben: We need to ensure no data exfiltration — is there per-request data tagging and retention controls?
[06:10] Lina: Yes, we have per-tenant retention settings, option to not log prompts/token payloads, redaction hooks, and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. We'll include the retention SLA in the security pack.
[06:24] Sofia: Can we test streaming and function-calling fidelity? Some of our pipelines parse the streaming JSON directly.
[06:30] Jonas: We'll provide a test harness that emits the same events so you can run end-to-end tests. Also, the SDK normalizes streaming chunking to be consistent.
[06:42] Tasha: Any limitations on model size or seq length?
[06:45] Jonas: We support long context models up to 128k tokens on dedicated capacity with appropriate kernel selection; for hosted tenants we have softer limits but can offer Dedicated for larger contexts.
[06:58] Arjun: If we choose Dedicated, what's the SLA and pricing model?
[07:02] Maya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with monthly commits. SLA is 99.9% for throughput targets; pricing depends on committed vGPU hours and model families. We'll send sample pricing scenarios.
[07:17] [07:30] Sofia: Regarding embeddings again — if recall drops, are there migration strategies?
[07:35] Jonas: Strategies: re-embed corpus, hybrid index (keep some vectors from old provider for cold queries), or apply a lightweight affine transform to align vector spaces if differences are linear — we can explore during pilot.
[07:50] Ben: Latency — initial tests vs OpenAI showed ~10-20ms differences in p50 on similar infra.
[07:57] Jonas: Latency depends on model and quantization and network egress. With Dedicated we can match or beat p50 by tuning kernel selection and batching. Optimize suggestions will include batching rules per route to hit your SLOs.
[08:14] Arjun: What about multi-region failover?
[08:18] Lina: Smart routing supports region failover and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; you can define prioritized regions and capacity tiers.
[08:30] Tasha: Do you support model version pinning? We want to avoid regressions during model upgrades.
[08:35] Maya: Yes — version pinning and staged rollouts with automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts tied to your evals. We also integrate with your eval harness via webhook.
[08:48] [09:05] Demo: Jonas runs a quick API parity example live: existing OpenAI call vs Redwood call. Jonas: See small diff — just change endpoint and a few headers, the payload mapping is 1:1 for most chat cases.
[09:26] Sofia: Are error codes the same? We have retry logic per-status.
[09:30] Jonas: Similar set — 429 rate limit, 5xx server errors; Redwood also emits per-token cost headers so you can measure unit economics.
[09:44] Ben: For private deployments, does Redwood support air-gapped on-prem?
[09:49] Lina: Yes, we have an on-prem package for regulated environments with offline control plane and local model hosting.
[09:58] Arjun: Ok, summary for us — we need parity mapping sheet, benchmark plan, security pack. When can you send?
[10:04] Maya: We'll send the docs by Friday (2026-04-02). Jonas will follow up with benchmark specifics.
[10:12] Tasha: Can we get a pilot environment with a test token?
[10:15] Maya: Yes — we can provide a short-lived pilot token and a pre-provisioned Dedicated trial if needed; we'll scope in the benchmark plan.
[10:22] Sofia: One more nuance — our pipeline uses tool-calling with nested JSON args; any limitations?
[10:27] Jonas: Nested JSON args are supported, but streaming semantics for very large arg blobs may require chunking. We'll provide patterns to keep things robust.
[10:36] Arjun: Are there any migration blockers you've seen in past customers?
[10:40] Maya: Mostly embeddings distribution shifts and some tooling differences for function calling. Both solvable with pilot runs and small SDK adaptors.
[10:51] [11:10] Wrap-up: Maya: recap next steps (parity doc, bench plan, security pack), set tentative pilot kickoff for next Tue.
[11:22] Ben: Thanks all, we'll send prompt set by Friday.
[11:26] Sofia: Appreciate the demo, looking forward to the parity sheet.
[11:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[11:35] End of recording.
